testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Posted heights at bridges:
questions.correctAnswerText: May be wrong.
questions.explanation: Do not assume posted heights are correct. Even if accurate when posted, conditions change. Road repaving or snow can affect clearance.

questions.question: What should you do if your brakes cannot build hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear.
questions.explanation: If your brakes will not build pressure, try shifting to a lower gear, pumping the brakes, or using the emergency brake.

questions.question: A high center of gravity in cargo:

options.text: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
Makes items fall down more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes the vehicle more likely to roll over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity increases rollover risk. Load cargo with safe weight distribution.

questions.question: To avoid slowing traffic in a large truck, you should:

options.text: Pass other vehicles while driving uphill.
Stay in the right lane as much as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the right lane as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If your heavy load cannot keep up with traffic speed, stay in the right lane.

questions.question: You may be driving aggressively if you:

options.text: Plan for delays on your drive.
Slow down and keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Make hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make hand gestures at other drivers.
questions.explanation: Avoid aggressive driving by planning for delays, keeping safe following distances, and not making hand gestures at other drivers.

questions.question: Regrooved tires:

options.text: Cannot be used on any vehicle.
Cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.
Cannot be used on trucks carrying gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cannot be used on the front wheels of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: Always do pre-trip inspection steps in the same order because:

options.text: You are less likely to forget a step.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are less likely to forget a step.
questions.explanation: Using the same order for inspection steps every time helps you remember all steps and learn the proper procedure.

questions.question: A lane change should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Done slowly.
questions.explanation: Make lane changes slowly and smoothly.

questions.question: As a truck driver, you are responsible for all of the following, except:

options.text: Memorizing fire department phone numbers along your route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Memorizing fire department phone numbers along your route.
questions.explanation: You must inspect cargo, recognize poor weight balance, secure cargo properly, and ensure cargo does not block your view or access to emergency equipment. You do not need to memorize fire department numbers.

questions.question: Rust around wheel nuts may mean:
questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose.
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may indicate they are loose. Check wheel nut tightness if you see rust before driving.

questions.question: When do you start to feel the effects of alcohol?

options.text: When you reach the legal limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: After the first drink.
questions.explanation: Alcohol impairs you starting with the first drink. It is illegal and dangerous to drive while impaired by alcohol.

questions.question: How does talking on a hands-free phone affect driving?

options.text: It does not distract the driver.
It only distracts the driver if the driver is speaking.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can distract the driver.
questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but they still distract your mind. Talking to someone takes your mental focus away from driving.

questions.question: When you start a truck with a trailer, how do you know the ABS is not working?

options.text: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
The red light on the right side of the trailer flashes three times.
All the rear lights flash and then turn off.

questions.correctAnswerText: The yellow light on the left rear of the trailer stays on.
questions.explanation: When you start your engine, the lights on the dashboard should turn on and then turn off. If the ABS warning light stays on, the system is not working. On a truck with a trailer, a yellow light on the left rear of the trailer that stays on means the ABS system is not working properly.

questions.question: What should happen to the coolant temperature when you start your vehicle?

options.text: It should jump quickly from low to high.

questions.correctAnswerText: It should increase slowly.
questions.explanation: Check your gauges before you drive. After starting your engine, the coolant temperature should rise slowly to the normal operating temperature.

questions.question: What should you do before starting a vehicle inspection?

options.text: The inspection report does not matter.
Only review the report if you will have passengers in the vehicle.
Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Review the previous inspection report, if there is one.
questions.explanation: The first step is to review the last inspection report. Only sign the new report if any defects from the last report have been fixed.

questions.question: What type of vehicle do you need to supply for a driving test?

options.text: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
Any type of vehicle, even if it is different from the one you will use with your CDL.
The testing station will provide the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same type of vehicle you will drive with your CDL.
questions.explanation: You must take the skills test in the same type of vehicle you plan to drive. You are responsible for supplying the testing vehicle.

questions.question: If you must drive onto the shoulder in an emergency, what should you do?

options.text: Get both sets of wheels onto the shoulder.
Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay on the shoulder until your vehicle stops, if possible.
questions.explanation: Stay on the shoulder until you stop. Then signal, check your mirrors, and merge back into traffic. Do not brake hard on the shoulder if you are going faster than 20 mph. Try to keep one set of wheels on the pavement to stay in control.

questions.question: What happens if you exit your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test?

options.text: You get an extra point against your final score.
You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.

questions.correctAnswerText: You automatically fail the entire basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: You must face the vehicle and hold on with three points of contact when exiting. If the vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly will cause you to fail the entire basic control skills test.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle starts to hydroplane?
questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brakes.
questions.explanation: Do not brake if your vehicle hydroplanes. Instead, release the accelerator and push in the clutch. This will help you regain traction.

questions.question: Where should you place weight when loading cargo?
questions.correctAnswerText: As low as possible.
questions.explanation: A vehicle can tip over if its center of gravity is too high. To prevent this, spread your cargo weight evenly and keep it as low as possible.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to hydroplane, what should you do?

options.text: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
Push in the clutch and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal and push in the clutch.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle hydroplanes, release the gas pedal and push in the clutch to regain control.

questions.question: When stopping, how should you use the brake pedal?

options.text: Press it down quickly with both feet.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press it down slowly.
questions.explanation: Press the brake pedal down slowly to stop smoothly and safely.

questions.question: Are pre-trip inspections required?

options.text: Only for trips longer than 100 miles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, the law requires them.
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require you to inspect your vehicle before every trip, no matter how short.

questions.question: What condition should the engine belts be in?
questions.correctAnswerText: Free of excessive wear.
questions.explanation: Check your engine belts for tightness and wear. Different belts may have different safe levels of give, so know what is right for your vehicle.

questions.question: If the previous driver left an inspection report, what should you do?

options.text: Skip your own inspection and use their report.
Take the vehicle to a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Read the report.
questions.explanation: Start your vehicle inspection by reviewing any report left by the previous driver.

questions.question: What are you not allowed to do while driving?

options.text: Make phone calls by pressing more than one button.
Hold a phone to make a voice call.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold a phone to make a voice call.
questions.explanation: While driving, you cannot send texts or hold a phone to call. You also cannot press more than one button on a phone to dial.

questions.question: What does a retarder do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slows down a vehicle.
questions.explanation: Retarders help slow vehicles so drivers do not have to use the brakes as much.

questions.question: What is true about carrying livestock?

options.text: Animals should be placed in the front of the trailer.
It can make the vehicle harder to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can make the vehicle harder to control.
questions.explanation: Livestock can shift and lean during turns, making the weight unstable. Driving with livestock requires extra care.

questions.question: If you are convicted of a traffic violation, what must you do?

options.text: Wait for the state to tell your employer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell your employer.
questions.explanation: You must tell your employer of any traffic conviction within 30 days. This rule does not apply to parking tickets.

questions.question: What can happen if a tire has too much air pressure?

options.text: It is not possible to overinflate a tire.
It is good for long drives.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be unsafe.
questions.explanation: Never overinflate your tires. Check tire air pressure with a gauge during inspections.

questions.question: Dry bulk tanks usually have:

options.text: Are usually not allowed to cross railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: High centers of gravity.
questions.explanation: Dry bulk tanks have high centers of gravity. The load weight can also shift during driving. Both of these factors require special driving care.

questions.question: How do you check hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should move slowly toward the floor.
Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should slowly rise.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Then push hard on the pedal for five seconds. The pedal should not move.
questions.explanation: Pump the brake pedal three times and then press hard for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it moves, there may be a leak or another brake system problem.

questions.question: Some air brake systems add alcohol to:

options.text: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
Prevent people from breathing air from the system.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent ice from forming in the brake system.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the system to stop ice from forming in cold weather.

questions.question: Non-front tires on a commercial truck must have a tread depth of at least:
questions.correctAnswerText: 2/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Front tires need 4/32 of an inch tread depth in every major groove. Other tires need 2/32 of an inch tread depth.

questions.question: A driver must ensure that:

options.text: The cargo is mostly in the front of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck is properly loaded.
questions.explanation: Cargo must be properly loaded for safe operation. Improper loading can hurt handling and damage the vehicle. It can also cause cargo to fall and injure or kill people.

questions.question: Backing with a trailer is dangerous because:

options.text: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
Most trucks cannot go in reverse.
Cargo may fall out of the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to see behind the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. Only back up if absolutely necessary.

questions.question: When loading cargo, it is important to:

options.text: Stack items as high as possible.
Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
Place light items under heavier items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Know the weight capacity of the suspension system.
questions.explanation: You must make sure your vehicle is not overloaded. Know the legal weight limits and the maximum weight your vehicle can carry, including its suspension system capacity.

questions.question: In icy conditions, a retarder should be:

options.text: Only used on the rear wheels.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turned off.
questions.explanation: A retarder can cause a skid when roads are icy or traction is poor. Turn it off in these conditions.

questions.question: Which gas from a faulty exhaust system is dangerous?
questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide
questions.explanation: A leaking exhaust system can let carbon monoxide into the cab or sleeper. Carbon monoxide is poisonous.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: After every trip.
questions.explanation: Do an after-trip inspection at the end of each trip, day, or duty period. Complete a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the other driver.
Assume the other driver does not see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume the other driver does not see you.
questions.explanation: Always assume that drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians do not see you. This is a safe driving practice.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when do you receive points?

options.text: If you cross over exercise boundaries.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cross over exercise boundaries.
questions.explanation: Each time your vehicle touches or crosses a boundary line, the examiner counts it as an error. These errors reduce your test score.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, air pressure should build from 85 to 100 psi within how many seconds?
questions.explanation: When checking a dual air brake system, wait for air pressure to build from 85 to 100 psi in both systems. This should take about 45 seconds.

questions.question: What is true about hanging meat as cargo?

options.text: It should never be transported by trailer.
It can be an unstable load.
It must be approved by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be an unstable load.
questions.explanation: Hanging meat is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and swings during transport. This affects how you handle the vehicle. Drive carefully with this type of load.

questions.question: How can a driver stay alert while driving?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stay fit and healthy.
questions.explanation: Heavy foods and a warm cab make you drowsy. Exercise and healthy eating help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: How long should it take for oil pressure to reach normal level when starting a vehicle?
questions.correctAnswerText: A few seconds.
questions.explanation: Oil pressure should reach normal level within seconds after starting the engine. Do not drive if oil pressure is low, dropping, or unstable.

questions.question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, what should a driver do?

options.text: Watch for people exiting a vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for people exiting a vehicle.
questions.explanation: People may step out of parked vehicles without looking. Drivers may also start moving their vehicle without seeing you. Be cautious and watch for these dangers.

questions.question: If your personal vehicle license is revoked or suspended, what happens to your CDL?

options.text: You can get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
You cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
Your CDL will not be affected.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.
questions.explanation: If your personal vehicle license is revoked, canceled, or suspended, you cannot get a hardship license to operate a CMV.

questions.question: If the spring brakes are on, what should you do?

options.text: Do not use the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not use the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: Do not use the brake pedal when spring brakes are on. This can damage the brakes by putting too much force on them.

questions.question: How should you test the low pressure warning signal?

options.text: Turn on the engine and apply the trailer hand brake.
Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
Remove wheel chocks and disengage the parking brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Rapidly press and release the brake pedal.
questions.explanation: After the air system is fully charged, rapidly press and release the brake pedal. This releases air from the system, and the warning light should come on when pressure drops to a dangerous level.
